items.config: Retain the proposed FW-only recipes, with adoption gated on outgoing-request inspection and lane A/B. Common contract: loopback /v1 endpoint; nonsecret SDK placeholder key; model=cx/gpt-6-astra-max; reasoning_effort=max; X-OmniRoute-No-Cache=true; X-OmniRoute-Compression=off; omit temperature/top_p. Direct SDK: timeout=3660; distinct stable sid per logical run, supplied through X-Session-Id and prompt_cache_key. Hindsight v0.10.1: retain the proposed openai provider/base URL/model/header/timeout variables, explicit openai_prompt_cache_key affinity, all five temperature settings=none, and operation-override audit. Cognee v1.6.1: retain litellm_native, LLM_PROVIDER=openai, LLM_MODEL=openai/cx/gpt-6-astra-max and the proposed LLM_ARGS; use a separate run identity per independently configured worker; leave LLM_TEMPERATURE unset. Keep Cognee strict-schema adoption gated. Preserve native CX settings, local embeddings, compression.enabled=false and exclusions=[codex/*]. Recipes were not installed.

findings.claim: The max-effort selection is supported; a suffix protects against wrapper-injected medium, subject to server force rules.
findings.evidence: gpt-6-astra belongs to the supported max/ultra alias sets. Codex resolves forced effort before model suffix, nested reasoning.effort, flat reasoning_effort and connection/default effort. The supplied snapshot records thinking-budget passthrough. No material defect was found in this control.

findings.claim: Keeping the compression master disabled and Codex excluded is necessary for the proposed default-path protection.
findings.evidence: The master gate precedes header selection. Provider/model exclusion disables both prompt compression and reactive compaction; header off disables only the selected prompt-compression plan. With the master enabled and exclusion removed, non-native FW requests can undergo reactive context trimming. The proposal correctly refuses to treat header off as complete isolation.

findings.claim: The SDK placeholder is compatible with keyless mode and creates no authentication or lane-isolation boundary.
findings.evidence: When REQUIRE_API_KEY is disabled, an invalid bearer degrades to anonymous access. Thus the placeholder avoids an SDK configuration requirement without adding protection to the existing loopback service; the proposal does not change gateway exposure.

findings.claim: Explicit cache bypass addresses a real fidelity risk and does not disable provider prompt caching.
findings.evidence: Legacy cache reads and writes honor X-OmniRoute-No-Cache=true. Explicit temperature=0 otherwise permits caching, although Codex removes temperature/top_p upstream. The legacy signature includes tools and output-format constraints but omits reasoning effort. The bypass is therefore justified independently of any token-saving claim.

findings.claim: Stable per-run identities support affinity without establishing measured savings or guaranteed cache hits.
findings.evidence: Account affinity recognizes the proposed header and falls back to body prompt_cache_key. FW translation preserves prompt_cache_key, and Codex preserves a supplied value. These controls do not themselves rewrite prompt text. The proposal correctly claims no measured savings against the approximately 94% cached-input baseline.

unverified: Installed OpenAI SDK, Hindsight, Cognee and LiteLLM versions; effective operation/call overrides; actual emitted model, effort, headers, prompt_cache_key, tools and response_format. Primary framework sources were inspected, but no deployed client was exercised.
Strict-schema recognition and preservation for the gateway alias, including schema demotion or prompt augmentation on retries; the proposal's adoption gate remains necessary.
Lane-specific correctness, cache continuity, token costs, retry behavior and complete client/gateway deadline envelope; no inference or A/B was performed.

items.config: Retain the installed numerical settings: OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=16384; CODEX_CLIENT_VERSION=0.157.1; STREAM_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS=600000; STREAM_READINESS_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=600000; STREAM_ACTIVE_TIMEOUT_MS=3600000; CLI_ALLOW_CONFIG_WRITES=false. Correct their documented scope: readiness waits for a qualifying non-ping event, including lifecycle-only events; a separate post-handoff first-model-content watchdog receives the adaptive readiness budget; the active-stream clock starts in the post-readiness pipeline. These are separate phases, not one ten-minute end-to-end first-content deadline. Preserve the 600000ms idle source default pending effective-environment verification. At the next reviewed deployment, explicitly require effective OMNIROUTE_SEMANTIC_CACHE_ENABLED=false. Retain compression.enabled=false, defaultMode=off, exclusions=[codex/*], liveZone.enabled=false, preserveSystemPromptMode=always and cacheMinutes=5; keep the pipeline breaker unset/false with no explicit true override. Leave admission auto-sizing and worker defaults unchanged. No settings were applied.

findings.claim: The proposed ten-minute first-content characterization is materially inaccurate; the state and numerical configuration can stand.
findings.evidence: Readiness accepts response.created and other non-ping lifecycle frames without real model output. After that handoff, chatCore supplies a separate content-stall budget to pipeWithDisconnect, which starts both content and active timers anew. Sequential readiness and content waits can therefore add together; the one-hour active budget also excludes preceding readiness and handler waits. This distinction matters when assessing max-effort truncation and client deadlines.

findings.claim: Retaining the service resource baseline is supported; configured heap size does not establish effective heap or concurrency capacity.
findings.evidence: Local read-only observation: installed and recorded units match, including the proposed six explicit values. Source permits 16384MB, calibrates an unset limit to approximately 35% of RAM within 512–4096MB, and preserves an existing NODE_OPTIONS heap flag in the serve launcher. REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS does not supply the active-stream default. The proposal correctly leaves effective memory and load capacity unverified.

findings.claim: Worker lifecycle and fallback claims support leaving workers unchanged while compression is disabled.
findings.evidence: The pool is lazy, eligibility is restricted, and idle removal explicitly terminates the worker. Ordinary worker faults may rerun compression in process; dispatch-timeout faults return the uncompressed body instead. Static resolution succeeded for the installed bundle's external dependencies, but this did not start a worker or establish initialization, execution or sustained memory health.

findings.claim: The vector-cache environment flag complements L04's bypass; resource retention has no demonstrated direct token benefit.
findings.evidence: OMNIROUTE_SEMANTIC_CACHE_ENABLED overrides vector-cache enablement, while the handler separately falls back to the legacy cache. Supplied snapshot observation: vector cache disabled, legacy cache enabled but empty, compression disabled with 1600 excluded requests and zero savings. Retaining those gates avoids new compression-induced prefix changes; avoided retries remain an unmeasured benefit.

unverified: Effective process environment, NODE_OPTIONS, goal-policy timeout overrides, actual V8 heap, cgroup ceiling, peak RSS, admission pressure and worker count; protected environment/auth stores were not read.
Worker startup, transitive/native initialization, engine execution, idle-cycle memory recovery and representative concurrent max-effort capacity.
The complete per-lane timeout envelope and legitimate single-turn duration requirements; the unchanged numerical limits are not an end-to-end duration guarantee.
